html:
Sachin Tendulkar is an Indian cricketer who scored more runs than anyone in the history of the international game. From 1989 to 2013 he was the most famous person in India.

He was born in Bombay in 1973, the son of a Marathi poet and teacher. As a schoolboy he practised for hours each day, and his coach would put a coin on the stumps for any bowler who could get him out. He first played for India at sixteen, in Pakistan in 1989. A ball from a fast bowler bloodied his nose in that series, and he batted on.

His records:

  • 200 Test matches, the only player to reach that number;
  • 15,921 runs in Tests and 18,426 in one-day internationals, both the highest ever;
  • 100 international centuries.

He stood about 1.65 metres tall and played every stroke. Crowds chanted his name, and many people switched off the television when he was out.

His career ran alongside India's opening to the world (see economic liberalisation). Satellite television and advertising made cricket rich, and India became the centre of the sport's money (see the Indian Premier League).

He won the World Cup at his sixth attempt in 2011, in his home city. He retired in 2013 and was the first sportsman given the Bharat Ratna.
sum: Sachin Tendulkar is an Indian cricketer who scored more runs than anyone in the history of the international game. From 1989 to 2013 he was the most famous person in India.
